title: Main statement (statements/S<NN>-<slug>.yaml)
description: One file per main statement: a theorem or an established physics result that several papers state in different notations. A node {"x-vocab": "<field>"} is expanded by scripts/validate.py from schema/vocab.yaml. Text limits are checked by the validator. A statement with public: false is a placeholder that stays out of the site; it must not hold the unpublished content (see INGEST.md, section Statements).

kind.description: collapse: several papers' results are one formula, shown to be equivalent under a mapping of symbols. grouping: a shared object or setting without an equivalence proof (the members are placed together, not shown equal).

family.description: Optional: the literature family the statement belongs to, e.g. rg for the renormalisation-group papers.

sense.description: Only for family rg: in which of the five senses the statement is a renormalisation statement (a to e).

maturity.description: Only for family rg: how far the RG reading is developed.

claim.description: One line: what the statement says. LaTeX allowed.

formula.description: The master formula, LaTeX in $...$ or $$...$$.

formula_note.description: What the symbols in the formula are, in the map's notation.

width_limit.description: Where the statement sits on the limit plane: one value of the width / limit field.

conditions.description: Dials and hypotheses under which it holds: P against N, scaling of the likelihood, temperature, activation, depth.

status_note.description: Which parts are proved and which are physics.

paper.description: arXiv ID without version (quoted), doi:<DOI>, or ref:<slug>.

result.description: Result id in that paper's entry (r1...r5). Omit when the whole paper is a member and no single result carries it.

statement.description: The paper's result as it reads in the map's notation.

mapping.description: Symbols of the paper in the statement's symbols.

equations.description: Equation, theorem or section numbers in the version read.

reduces_to.description: Other statements this one reduces to, and the limit that connects them (direction: this statement, in that limit, becomes the target).

conjectural.description: true when the connection lies outside the hypotheses of the cited theorems; the graph draws the arrow dashed.

open_problems.description: Open problems that sit next to this statement (op-NN).

links.description: Optional relations to other statements that are not reduces_to: an analogy, the same object in another language, a shared method.
